back: Add dilute acid: effervescence; the gas (carbon dioxide) turns limewater milky.
Acidify with dilute nitric acid, add aqueous silver nitrate: white precipitate.
Acidify with dilute nitric acid, add aqueous silver nitrate: yellow precipitate.
Acidify with dilute nitric acid, add aqueous silver nitrate: cream precipitate.
Acidify with dilute nitric acid, add aqueous barium nitrate: white precipitate.
notes: Also used: dilute hydrochloric acid and barium chloride.

back: Add aqueous sodium hydroxide and aluminium foil, warm: ammonia given off (damp red litmus turns blue).
Add acidified aqueous potassium manganate(VII): purple to colourless.

front: Why acidify before the halide and sulfate tests?
back: To remove carbonate ions, which would also give precipitates with silver or barium ions.

front: Which acids must not be used to acidify?
back: Not hydrochloric acid for the chloride test (adds Cl⁻); not sulfuric acid for the sulfate test (adds SO₄²⁻).

front: Ionic equation for the chloride test
